info.title: Recoup API - Research
info.description: API documentation for the Recoup platform - an AI agent platform for the music industry

get.description: Returns chats for the authenticated account. Personal Bearer tokens see only the caller's chats; org keys see chats across the org's member accounts; admin keys see all chats. Each row carries the chat id and the session id needed to build the chat URL.

parameters.name: artist_account_id
parameters.description: Optional. Filter chats to only include those whose owning session's `artistId` matches the supplied artist account id. Combine with `account_id` to scope by both owner and artist.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: Filter to a specific account. Only applicable when the authenticated account has access to multiple accounts via organization membership.

401.description: Unauthorized - invalid or missing API key

403.description: Forbidden - account_id is not a member of the organization or account tried to filter by an account_id they don't have access to

post.description: Create a new chat room. Optionally associate it with an artist and/or provide a client-generated chat ID. Pass accountId to create a chat on behalf of a specific account the API key has access to.

post.description:
Start an asynchronous, headless chat-generation run on the durable agent workflow — the same engine as interactive [`POST /api/chat`](/api-reference/chat/workflow).

**Related endpoints**
- [`POST /api/chat`](/api-reference/chat/workflow) — use that for **interactive, streaming** turns on an existing chat; use this for **headless/programmatic** runs (no browser or pre-provisioned session needed).
- [`GET /api/chat/runs/{runId}`](/api-reference/chat/runs-status) — poll to learn **whether** the run finished (and if it succeeded).
- [`GET /api/chat/{chatId}/stream`](/api-reference/chat/workflow-stream) — **watch the output live** by passing the returned `chatId`.

202.description: Run accepted. A durable workflow run was started; `runId` identifies it. `chatId` / `sessionId` identify the persisted output — read the result via [`GET /api/chat/{chatId}/stream`](/api-reference/chat/workflow-stream) (resume the stream) or the chat's persisted messages. Poll [`GET /api/chat/runs/{runId}`](/api-reference/chat/runs-status) for status.

Location.description: Relative URL of the run-status resource for the started run.

post.description:
Stop the response currently being generated for a chat, freeing it to accept a new message. Idempotent — returns `stopped: false` when nothing is in progress. The chat must belong to the authenticated account.

The active slot is released only after cancellation is confirmed. Cancellation failure (502) or termination timeout (504) keeps it occupied; a later stop can retry. A successful no-active stop returns stopped: false.

When a workflow is still starting and has no cancellable run ID, Stop returns retryable `503` and retains the active reservation. It does not report `stopped: true`; retry Stop shortly. A local reader abort is not confirmation that server work stopped.

For readers using `streamLifecycle=explicit-stop-v1`, this authenticated endpoint remains the explicit cancellation path.

parameters.name: chatId
parameters.description: UUID of the chat to stop.

200.description: No active workflow exists (`stopped: false`), or cancellation and terminal status were confirmed (`stopped: true`). A pending start returns 503 instead of successful cancellation.

400.description: chatId is not a valid UUID

403.description: The chat belongs to a different account

404.description: Chat not found

401.description: Missing or invalid authentication.

500.description: Session ownership lookup failed.

502.description: Workflow cancellation failed; the active slot remains held.

504.description: Workflow did not reach a terminal state before the wait deadline; the active slot remains held.

503.description: Workflow start has reserved the chat but has not returned a cancellable run ID. The reservation remains held, and cancellation is not confirmed. Retry Stop shortly.

pendingStart.summary: Stop requested before the workflow run ID is available

value.error: Workflow is still starting; retry Stop shortly

get.description:
Reconnects to an in-progress chat response without submitting another message. POST /api/chat starts a new turn: an existing live run returns 409, while uncertain state or a startup reservation returns retryable 503. Returns a live Server-Sent Events stream while a response is being generated, or a `200` finish-only SSE stream when no active response exists or the run is terminal. The chat must belong to the authenticated account.

Send `?streamLifecycle=explicit-stop-v1` on both the initial POST and this reconnect GET to keep server work running when a reader disconnects. Use the authenticated Stop endpoint for cancellation; closing or aborting this reader alone does not confirm that the workflow stopped. Only exactly one streamLifecycle parameter with the exact value opts in; omitted, empty, unknown or repeated parameters retain legacy disconnect cancellation. Keep the existing `startIndex` cursor when reconnecting an already-read response.

**Related endpoints**
- [`POST /api/chat`](/api-reference/chat/workflow) — the interactive turn whose stream this resumes.
- [`POST /api/chat/runs`](/api-reference/chat/runs) — start a **headless** run, then pass the returned `chatId` here to **watch its output live**.
- [`GET /api/chat/runs/{runId}`](/api-reference/chat/runs-status) — check **whether** that run finished (status, not content).

parameters.name: chatId
parameters.description: UUID of the chat to resume.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: Act on a chat belonging to another account. Only honoured for a key that is authorised for that account — an organization key may pass a member account's id; a personal key passing anyone else's is rejected with `403 Access denied to specified account_id`. Omit it to act as the authenticated account.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:
Zero-based index of the first stream chunk to return, so a client that was already receiving this response resumes where it left off instead of replaying the whole turn.

Pass the number of chunks already received. Omit it to receive the response from the beginning — the right choice for a fresh reader such as a page load, or a client watching a headless [`POST /api/chat/runs`](/api-reference/chat/runs) run for the first time.

A long turn's stream can end before the run does; reconnecting with `startIndex` is how a client keeps rendering without duplicating or skipping chunks.

parameters.name: streamLifecycle
parameters.description: Send streamLifecycle=explicit-stop-v1 exactly once on the initial POST and every reconnect GET to keep server work running when that reader disconnects. Only exactly one parameter with that exact value opts in. Omitting it, an empty or unknown value, or repeating the parameter retains legacy disconnect cancellation. Use authenticated POST /api/chat/{chatId}/stop for cancellation; a local reader abort is not confirmation that server work stopped. This is a query parameter, not a request-body field.

200.description: Server-Sent Events stream of UI message parts for the in-progress response, compatible with the Vercel AI SDK. The `x-workflow-run-id` response header carries the run ID for this response, and `x-workflow-stream-tail-index` carries the index of the last chunk known when this read was opened — a base for computing absolute positions, not a record of where the response ended. When there is nothing to resume, the stream contains one terminal finish chunk; workflow headers are absent on that path.

x-workflow-run-id.description: Durable workflow run ID of the resumed run.

x-workflow-stream-tail-index.description: Zero-based index of the last chunk known to the stream **at the moment this read was opened**. Because headers are sent before the body, a read that stays open past that point will deliver chunks beyond it — so this is a base for computing absolute positions, not a record of where the response ended. A client resuming precisely should count the chunks it receives on top of this value. Omitted if the runtime cannot report it.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events stream containing UI message parts

400.description: Invalid chatId UUID or malformed startIndex. When supplied, startIndex must parse to a non-negative integer; blank, nonnumeric, fractional and negative values fail validation. Authentication/ownership is checked first. Validation errors include status: error, error and missing_fields when a validation path is available.

401.description: Missing or invalid authentication.

403.description: The caller does not own the chat session.

404.description: Chat or owning session not found.

500.description: The chat or session ownership lookup failed. This is not a missing-chat result.

502.description: Workflow status lookup failed; this is not an empty or completed response.

post.description:
Streams an agent loop running as a durable [Vercel Workflow](https://vercel.com/docs/workflow) against the session's sandbox. The agent uses sandbox-only tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `grep`, `glob`, `todo`, `task`, `ask_user_question`, `skill`, `fetch`) — no MCP or Composio. Requires a sandbox provisioned via [`POST /api/sandbox`](/api-reference/sandbox/create).

**Related endpoints**
- [`POST /api/chat/runs`](/api-reference/chat/runs) — the **headless** counterpart: it provisions its own session + sandbox and runs without a streaming client. Use that for tasks/cron/programmatic runs; use this for **interactive, streaming** turns on an existing chat.
- [`GET /api/chat/{chatId}/stream`](/api-reference/chat/workflow-stream) — reconnect to an in-progress response.
- [`GET /api/chat/runs/{runId}`](/api-reference/chat/runs-status) — check **whether** a headless run finished (status, not content).

A new turn is separate from reconnecting. If the early active-run check finds an existing run whose status is running or pending, POST returns `409` before saving the new message or starting a new workflow. Keep the rejected text and attachments locally, reconnect with GET, and let the caller decide when to submit them again. Do not queue or automatically resend them, or delete persisted chat history to recover an unaccepted submission. Later start conflicts can also return `409` after work has started; inspect chat state before retrying. An unresolved startup reservation, unknown run status, failed status lookup or failed stale-slot clear returns retryable `503` before saving the submitted turn or starting a new workflow. Preserve the text and attachments for a later manual retry.

To make a reader disconnect leave the workflow running, send `?streamLifecycle=explicit-stop-v1` on this POST and every reconnect GET. Use `POST /api/chat/{chatId}/stop` for explicit cancellation; aborting the local reader is not confirmation that server work stopped. Only exactly one streamLifecycle query parameter with that exact value opts in. Omitted, empty, unknown or repeated parameters retain legacy disconnect cancellation.

200.description: Server-Sent Events stream of UI message parts for the newly started workflow, compatible with the Vercel AI SDK `createUIMessageStreamResponse`. The `x-workflow-run-id` response header carries the durable workflow run ID for resume/stop operations. An existing active response is rejected with 409 instead of being returned as acceptance of the submitted new message.

x-workflow-run-id.description: Durable workflow run ID. Persist alongside the chat so a later `GET /api/chat/{chatId}/stream` request can resume this run after a disconnect.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events stream containing UI message parts

400.description: Bad request — missing required fields, invalid body, or sandbox not initialized for the session.

401.description: Missing or invalid API key.

403.description: The API key's account does not own the referenced `sessionId` or `chatId`.

404.description: Session or chat not found.

409.description: A response is already active, a concurrent request claimed the chat, or another conflict prevented this start. The early active-run rejection does not save the submitted message or start a new workflow. Later conflicts may occur after work starts. Preserve rejected text and attachments, inspect chat state and use GET /api/chat/{chatId}/stream to reconnect before a manual retry; no automatic replay is performed.

500.description: Server error, including a failed chat or session lookup. A failed lookup is not a missing-chat result.

503.description: Run state cannot be resolved safely, including an unresolved startup reservation, unknown status, failed status lookup or failed stale-slot clear. A pending startup reservation remains held. The early rejection does not save the submitted turn or start a new workflow. Keep the text and attachments for a later manual retry; no automatic replay.

parameters.name: streamLifecycle
parameters.description: Send streamLifecycle=explicit-stop-v1 exactly once on the initial POST and every reconnect GET to keep server work running when that reader disconnects. Only exactly one parameter with that exact value opts in. Omitting it, an empty or unknown value, or repeating the parameter retains legacy disconnect cancellation. Use authenticated POST /api/chat/{chatId}/stop for cancellation; a local reader abort is not confirmation that server work stopped. This is a query parameter, not a request-body field.

post.description: Create a current capture or enqueue historical the configured research data connection backfill. Provide exactly one of catalog_id, album_ids or isrcs in scope; platforms supports spotify only. source=current uses the snapshot pipeline and returns an ID that can be passed to [Create catalog](/api-reference/songs/catalogs-create). source=historical requires a card on file, resolves scope recordings and returns id:null with enqueued/skipped counts; it attempts to start the existing budget-gated backfill workflow, with daily maintenance as a backstop. Enqueue success is not capture completion or evidence of complete historical coverage. Songs with any historical research measurement are skipped, including potentially partial history. Historical enqueue itself makes no credit deduction; current capture estimates and provider/account gates remain separate.

400.description: Invalid scope/source/platform, or no recordings resolvable from the selected historical scope.

401.description: Authentication failed — invalid or missing API key.

402.description: Historical backfill requires a saved payment method. Unlike the ordinary research credit gate, this gate creates a card-setup Checkout Session per denied request and returns checkoutUrl; do not repeatedly submit to poll this error.

checkoutUrl.description: Card-setup checkout URL returned by Stripe. Distinct from the static billingUrl used by ordinary research credit errors.

500.description: Internal, enqueue or provider configuration error.

get.description:
Status of an asynchronous run started via [`POST /api/chat/runs`](/api-reference/chat/runs). Returns a point-in-time snapshot (**is it done?**) — not the generated content.

**Related endpoints**
- [`POST /api/chat/runs`](/api-reference/chat/runs) — starts the run this reports on.
- [`GET /api/chat/{chatId}/stream`](/api-reference/chat/workflow-stream) — read the **content**: poll *this* to know **whether** a run finished; use the stream to **watch the output** as it's produced.
- [`POST /api/chat`](/api-reference/chat/workflow) — the interactive, streaming counterpart to a headless run.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: The durable workflow run id returned by [POST /api/chat/runs](/api-reference/chat/runs).

404.description: Run not found

get.description:
Search Recoup Research for artists, tracks or labels by name. Artist and track matches include an `id` when an identifier is available. Select a match and reuse that ID for detail requests. `type` accepts artists, tracks or labels, plus their singular aliases, case-insensitively. Playlist search is unavailable. Recoup defaults `limit` to 10; pagination strings are passed to the data connection and its limits apply.

Use your Recoup API key (`x-api-key`) or supported bearer credential. Successful artist and track research reads cost $0.05 (50,000 micro-dollar credits). Recoup manages the data connections. Coverage and rate limits vary; see [Research availability](/research-availability).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Required search text, such as an artist or track name. For a Spotify artist URL use the lookup endpoint.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Entity type to search: artists, tracks, or labels.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Raw pagination string forwarded to the configured research data connection. Recoup defaults limit to 10; offset is omitted when absent. Provider limits apply.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Raw pagination string forwarded to the configured research data connection. Recoup defaults limit to 10; offset is omitted when absent. Provider limits apply.

401.description: Authentication failed — invalid or missing API key

402.description: Insufficient research credits. The response includes a static billingUrl; no checkout session is created.

403.description: Credential, account or provider permission denied.

404.description: Artist/track resolution or requested provider data was not found. A failed name search may be reported as 404; retry with an exact provider ID when known.

500.description: Missing provider configuration, transport failure or internal error.

504.description: the configured research data connection request timed out.

Results can include track-shaped catalog entries rather than distinct album objects. `is_primary` accepts true/false; filtering depends on the data connection. `limit` must be a positive integer string and `offset` a non-negative integer string.

Use your Recoup API key (`x-api-key`) or supported bearer credential. Successful artist and track research reads cost $0.05 (50,000 micro-dollar credits). Recoup manages the data connections. Coverage and rate limits vary; see [Research availability](/research-availability).

Use your Recoup API key (`x-api-key`) or supported bearer credential. Successful artist and track research reads cost $0.05 (50,000 micro-dollar credits). Recoup manages the data connections. Coverage and rate limits vary; see [Research availability](/research-availability).

Other values must be one of the listed lowercase names. Invalid platform values return `400` before authentication, artist resolution, credit checks or research dispatch. Availability and returned coverage vary by platform.

snippet.description: Content snippet from the search result.

formatted.description: Results formatted as markdown for easy reading.

message.description: Error message describing what went wrong

ResearchEventsRequest.description: Request body for artist event lookup.

artist_id.description: Recoup artist id. Events are resolved through the live-events profile connected to this artist, so the lookup is exact and cannot drift to a same-named performer. Returns 404 if no live-events profile is connected.

events.description: Matching events, ascending by date. Empty when the artist has none.

region.description: State or region where the source provides one. US venues carry a state code such as "TN"; most non-US venues return an empty string, as in the example below.

country.description: Country name. Pair with `city` before filtering by market, since city names such as London and Paris are not unique across countries.

ticket_url.description: Ticket link where one is published.

sold_out.description: Whether the source marks the event sold out.

lineup.description: Billed artists, the queried artist first. More than one entry means a shared bill.

ResearchErrorResponse.description: Error response returned by all research endpoints for validation failures (400) and authentication errors (401).

error.description: Human-readable error message describing what went wrong.

ResearchTrackStatsResponse.description: Current per-source track statistics from the Spotify measurement store or the configured research data connection. Provider payloads and coverage vary; inspect per-entry provenance when present.

ResearchTrackStat.description: Per-source current statistics for a single track.

source.description: Requested provider platform (for example spotify or apple_music); coverage depends on provider entitlement.

data.description: Provider-specific track counters. A Spotify store streams_total is a platform-displayed play count, not a royalty-bearing stream count.

data_source.description: Opaque provenance label identifying the measurement origin. Preserve this value for traceability. Labels can vary with the data connection and are not a supported vendor selector. Missing provenance remains unknown.

captured_at.description: When this entry's values were captured into the measurement store.

ResearchInsufficientCreditsResponse.description: Returned (402) when the account lacks research credits. Nothing is charged and no Stripe object is created. Credits must be bought explicitly via [`POST /api/credits/sessions`](/api-reference/credits/sessions-create).

billingUrl.description: Static link to the Recoup app, where a human can save a card and buy credits. It is a constant, not a freshly minted Stripe Checkout Session, so a credit-gated endpoint that keeps returning 402 creates nothing. To buy credits programmatically, call [`POST /api/credits/sessions`](/api-reference/credits/sessions-create).

ResearchMeasurementsResponse.description: A track's measured series, or — when `aggregate` is set — the derived projection.

source.description: current captures present counts through the snapshot pipeline; historical enqueues the configured research data connection backfill. Historical requires a saved payment method and does not promise complete history.

state.description: State returned by the snapshot pipeline; reused captures need not be queued.

reused.description: Present when an existing capture is handed back.

id.description: No pollable snapshot ID is created for historical backfill.

enqueued.description: Recordings submitted to the backfill queue; this does not mean history is captured.

skipped.description: Recordings with any existing historical research measurement; skipping does not prove complete history.

ResearchMeasurementJobResponse.description: Current captures return a snapshot ID; historical backfill returns queue counts and id:null.

runId.description: Durable workflow run id for the started generation. Same identifier surfaced as the `x-workflow-run-id` header on interactive [POST /api/chat](/api-reference/chat/workflow).

chatId.description: Chat the run writes its assistant messages to. Use with [`GET /api/chat/{chatId}/stream`](/api-reference/chat/workflow-stream) to resume the stream, or to fetch the persisted messages.

sessionId.description: Session (workspace + sandbox) provisioned for the run.

ChatRunStatusResponse.description: Point-in-time status of an asynchronous chat-generation run.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the run. Read the produced content via the chat (`chatId` from the start response).

createdAt.description: When the workflow run was created; null if unavailable, including for terminal runs.

startedAt.description: When execution started; null while unavailable or if its timing getter fails, including for terminal runs.

completedAt.description: When the run reached a terminal state; null while unavailable or if its timing getter fails, including for terminal runs.

durationMs.description: completedAt minus startedAt in milliseconds; null if either timestamp is unavailable, including for terminal runs.

ResearchCatalogItem.description: Catalog entry. Unfiltered — high-catalog artists include remixes/features.

ResearchArtistMini.description: Minimal artist reference embedded in catalog/activity payloads.

ResearchSimilarResponse.description: Similar artists. Similarity is unweighted (no score/ranking fields).

total.description: Only present if the adapter receives a provider total; not guaranteed.

ResearchProfileResponse.description: Full artist profile. For longitudinal platform metrics call `GET /api/research/metrics`.

ResearchArtistInfo.description: Full artist record — identity, bio, genres, platform links, and related artists.

ResearchPlaylistPlacement.description: A playlist the artist currently appears on.

external_url.description: Link to the playlist on the platform.

ResearchMilestonesResponse.description: Milestone activity entries (same shape as career/insights).

ResearchActivity.description: Dated activity event. Shared by career, insights, and milestones.

ResearchActivityTrackInfo.description: Track context attached to an activity entry.

ResearchMetricsResponse.description: Current statistics for the artist on the requested `source`.

source.description: Platform the metrics belong to, e.g. `spotify`, `tiktok`.

data.description: Platform-specific metric fields. Keys vary by `source`.

ResearchLookupResponse.description: Artist resolved from a Spotify URL or ID.

id.description: Opaque Recoup research artist ID when resolved. Reuse it in artist research requests; it is separate from the Recoup artist account UUID and Spotify ID.

ResearchAudienceResponse.description: Provider audience payload. Available geographic and demographic fields vary by source and entitlement.

audience.description: Provider audience entries; fields vary by requested metric source. Empty data does not establish an absent audience.

results.description: Matching artists, tracks or labels with provider identifiers and metadata.

ResearchSearchResult.description: Search result. Additional type-specific identifier fields pass through. The set depends on `type` (artists | tracks | labels).

ResearchDataSourceUnsupported.description: The configured research data source does not support this endpoint or data shape.
